A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaFisher research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices A–D support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original image-classification, language-modeling, curvature-analysis, ablation, and computational-efficiency results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds optimizer comparisons and equal-epoch experiments, particularly in Appendix D.2.5–D.2.6.

M1.justification: Equation (3) and Algorithm 1 replace the two-coefficient Kronecker-factor update with a single-gamma EMA. Proposition 3.1 replaces the normalization-layer formulas with separate scale and shift factors. Appendix A.4 also changes aggregation from averaging normalized factors to normalizing aggregated factors. These revise the specified preconditioning procedure; the PDFs do not establish corresponding implementation changes or reruns.

E1.justification: Both use CIFAR10/100, Tiny ImageNet, ImageNet, WikiText-2, and PTB, plus MNIST and IRIS in supporting experiments. Transfer learning, distributed training, and the existing perturbation and augmentation scenarios are retained. New comparisons reuse existing datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated SGD comparisons to CIFAR training and transfer learning, and EVA and AdaFactor comparisons in Tables 14–15. ImageNet Table 3 additionally includes a literature-sourced AdamW result. The earlier ImageNet Momentum entries are renamed SGD, rather than constituting new comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2.6 adds a fixed 200-epoch protocol for ResNet-18, ResNet-50, and MobileNet-V3 on CIFAR100, supplementing the retained wall-clock-time comparisons. New comparator settings include 119 epochs for EVA and 216 for AdaFactor under the time budget, plus SGD training budgets and momentum tuning.

E4.justification: The new equal-epoch analysis examines whether accuracy and efficiency conclusions persist when epochs replace elapsed time as the matching criterion. Existing learning-rate, batch-size, scheduler, noise, EMA, square-root, normalization-layer, and Fisher-approximation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both specify five randomly initialized CIFAR trials with means and standard deviations, and one trial each for Tiny ImageNet and ImageNet. V3 introduces no new repeated-run, confidence-interval, or significance-testing procedure. Additional result entries do not establish a changed statistical practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds SGD, EVA, and AdaFactor outcomes and equal-epoch accuracy/runtime results. In the new ResNet-18/CIFAR100 comparison, Table 15 reports Shampoo at 77.35% versus AdaFisher at 77.28%, taking 216.67 versus 26.58 minutes. These are new-condition results, not changes in same-setting performance. Most existing headline means remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition A.1 replaces the normalization-layer derivation with separate scale/shift Fisher blocks and explicit cross-term exclusion. Proposition A.2 adds spectral bounds, invertibility reasoning, and an O(epsilon + lambda) relative inverse-error claim. Existing convergence-rate claims largely remain. The new scale-block derivation contains a dimensional mismatch between a C-by-C Fisher block and a Kronecker product of two C-by-C factors.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain the diagonal-Kronecker Fisher optimizer, its robustness and efficiency, superior image/language performance, and trajectory/Fisher visualizations. Abstract and conclusion refinements retain these claims rather than introducing a materially different contribution.

C2.justification: V3 adds an implicit-regularization interpretation, clarifies the exponential-family/negative-log-likelihood applicability boundary, and discusses nonsmooth network components and initialization variability. Appendix D.2.6 acknowledges Shampoo's slight accuracy advantage with substantially greater runtime, qualifying the performance interpretation.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses a 50-epoch CNN hyperparameter-search duration, adds SGD tuning details and settings for EVA/AdaFactor, and explicitly identifies AdamW/AdaFisherW use for ViTs. Algorithm defaults change from gamma1=0.92 and gamma2=0.0008 to gamma=0.8. Hardware and code-access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references and discussion covering EVA, AdaFactor, FOOF, Sophia, newer Kronecker preconditioning, and implicit regularization. These broaden contextual coverage while retaining the established positioning around tractable Fisher approximations and adaptive optimization. Publication updates and duplicate-reference consolidation do not represent new research coverage.

P1.justification: V3 edits the abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion; standardizes KF/HP terminology and time-index notation; renames Section 3.3; and adds two experimental appendix subsections. The main section sequence and most appendix narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: CIFAR and transfer-learning tables and plots expand to include SGD. V3 adds Tables 14–15 and Figures 21–22, combines v2 Figures 22–23 into Figure 23, revises the Fisher-computation diagram, and relocates several displays. The ImageNet display labeled Figure 5 in v2 becomes Table 3.

improvement.justification: Adding SGD/EVA/AdaFactor comparisons and an equal-epoch control strengthens the empirical evaluation beyond v2's wall-clock-time comparisons. The clearer applicability boundary also helps. The net gain is limited: broad superiority claims remain despite Table 15's Shampoo exception, and the rewritten normalization proof introduces a dimensional inconsistency, so the expanded mathematics does not establish stronger theoretical support.
